blocks.text: The catalogue is not merely a collection of names and numbers. Its family groups, priestly eligibility tests, servants, singers, animals, contributions, and totals together make an administrative and theological claim that the returned community stands in continuity with those who had previously come from captivity. Because some figures differ from the parallel list in Ezra 2, and because ancient counting practices remain uncertain, these totals should not be treated as a precise modern census without qualification.

sections.title: The Memoir within the Larger Book

blocks.text: The first-person account leading into this chapter belongs to what is often described as Nehemiah's memoir, with vivid reports of prayer, royal service, construction, opposition, and reform. Yet the completed book also contains third-person narration, genealogical lists, material involving Ezra, and editorial transitions. Its varied presentation therefore resists being reduced either to an uninterrupted autobiography or to a wholly fictional account.
